Admission binds one seat to one hull under a licensed jetty. The applicant signs a berth lease, a surveyor issues a hull survey with a photo of the welded plate number, and the node hashes plate against lease, re-reading the harbour register each quarter. One plate, one berth: a second lease on the same hull voids both.

Fifty clones need fifty hulls, the cheapest 12,000 dollars surveyed, berth 1,900 a quarter, survey 450, so a cohort clears half a million before a net lifts.

A thread holds at two knots; a marble rests because the table is level, and the plate is the level.
